findings.problem: In Latin America, alcanzar is a very common one-word verb for 'to be enough' (El dinero no alcanza), and the hint 'one verb' doesn't rule it out.
findings.fix: hint: one verb, also shouted on its own to mean 'Stop it!' (not alcanzar)

findings.problem: Here ¡Basta! is a fixed interjection meaning 'Stop it!', not the verb conjugated in a sentence with the meaning 'to be enough'.
findings.fix: example.es: Con un café me basta para empezar el día. example.en: One coffee is enough for me to start the day.

back.es: to be enough, to suffice (Spanish usually puts the thing that is enough as the subject: basta con eso, that's enough)
back.example: Enough! I don't want to talk about that anymore.

note: The interjection ¡Basta! is still worth teaching, maybe in the hint or as a second example, since learners hear it all the time in films and TV.
